title: Patchwork Handoff Notes (midwatch) - scratch draft
content:
Context / purpose:
Quick, messy midwatch notes — meant to be read in 2-5 minutes. Not a canonical runbook; patchwork of checks, heuristics, and short-term mitigations that I rely on at 03:00. Leave any additions here (mark "Aisha note" or "TODO").

Shift summary (what I saw before leaving):
- No active Sev1s. Brief blips on ratelimit proxy at 01:42 (see JIRA-INFRA-4231) — autoscaler recovered after ~4m.
- One degraded model route (~10% elevated latency) for model: gptx-7b-q4intel on cluster: eu-west-2-g1 (investigating kernel fallback logs).
- Alert noise: intermittent DNS lookup failures from monitoring agents; appears to be sporadic resolver timeout (ns-ops ticket filed).

Immediate checks (first 120s):
1) Pager overview: /alerts -> filter: open, severity >= P2, assigned to eng-sre.
2) k8s namespaces: kubectl get pods -n redwood-infer -o wide | grep Evicted
   - Quick check: if >3 evicted pods in last 10m, roll nodesets: infra/auto-replace script.
3) Model-serving health: curl -s https://status.internal.redwood/api/serving | jq .routes["gptx-7b-q4intel"]
   - If route shows "degraded", check node pool: kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -E "OOM|error|RestartCount"
4) Router queue length: redis-cli -h proxy-queue info | grep length
   - If > 10k, scale dedup/batcher or enable temporary backpressure: POST /ops/api/backpressure?duration=10m

Quick mitigation recipes (short-term, temporary):
- Model fallback: flip traffic to gptx-7b-8bit variant via rollout API (UI -> Routes -> Canary -> set weight 90%). Note: quantify cost change before committing.
- If autoscaler not reacting: restart controller: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/auto-scaler (watch logs).
- For DNS resolver flakiness: switch monitoring agents to fallback resolver (127.0.0.2) via SSM parameter update; this lasts until engineers deploy fix.

Commands I frequently run (copy-paste safe-ish):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-infer --sort-by=.status.startTime -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood-infer svc/route-gateway -c gateway --since=15m | tail -n 200
- redis-cli -h proxy-queue LRANGE queue:requests 0 20
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_KEY" "https://ops.api.internal/v1/rollouts/route/gptx-7b" | jq .

Escalation / contacts (rapid):
- Tier1 (oncall SRE): #oncall (Slack) -> expect 5-10m response
- Tier2 (infra-ops): Mateo Ruiz (Slack: @mateo) -> for node/GPUs/EC2 capacity issues
- Model infra lead: Jing Wei (Slack: @jing) -> for model runtime regressions or quantization fallbacks
- Pager escalation: escalate to Eng Manager if unresolved > 30m or customer impact escalates

Known flaky areas + heuristics I use to triage quickly:
- Batcher stalls: if per-token latency rises but CPU/GPU utilization low -> suspect batcher deadlock. Quick test: tail batcher logs; if you see "flush timeout" >5, restart batcher pod.
- KV cache eviction spikes: sudden latency for long-context requests often correlates with cache misses. Look at cache hit-rate metric (console -> metrics -> cache_hit_rate).
- Quantization fallback: sometimes kernel pick fails and falls back to slower path. Logs show "kernel: fallback path activated". If happening across many pods, roll back recent kernel patch.

Temporary customer-facing mitigation (if routes degraded):
- Create temporary alias route with conservative settings: lower max_seq_len to 1024, lighter sampling temp, and use cached responses for identical prompt hashes (TTL 30m). Announce in #customers-impact if > 5% error rate.

Things I left TODO / followups for daytime team:
- (Aisha note) correlate autoscaler decision logs with instance launch times for INFRA-4231.
- (Priority) Dig into eu-west-2-g1 kernel selection telemetry — add histogram metric for fallback counts.
- Check with Platform Eng if recent kernel changes rolled to all clusters (ticket: PLAT-1120).
- Replace quickpatch DNS resolver with proper fix from ns-ops (blocked by ops-release).

Notes to successor (face-to-face handoff tips):
- If you see a fast-growing queue but CPU/GPU usage low, first suspect Router -> Batcher link; don't immediately scale GPU capacity or you'll pay/overprovision.
- When flipping traffic, always leave a 10% canary for 10 minutes and watch model quality metrics (eval-dashboard).
- If you restart something, annotate the restart in the alert ticket with reason and command used. Saves time for postmortem.

Post-incident artifacts to create (if incident happens):
- Short blameless timeline in JIRA ticket: who acted, what command, timestamps, and customer impact estimate.
- Quick slack summary in #incident-postmortems with link to raw logs (S3).

Rough checklist for handover completion:
- [ ] Verify no critical alerts assigned to eng-sre
- [ ] Confirm temporary mitigations (if any) are annotated and owner assigned
- [ ] Leave explicit next steps (this doc) and point to any created tickets

Misc bits (random notes I keep):
- If you need to test fallback locally, use the replica test cluster: test-serve-01; credentials in 1Password vault: "oncall/test-serve".
- Small trick: "curl --fail" will surface 5xx quickly in watch loops.

Signature: Aisha Khan (midwatch patchwork). Add your name and timestamp when you take over.

-- end --
